name: Bosch EDC17CP14 (VAG 2.0 TDI common rail)
eeprom: Emulated in the TC1796 128 KiB data flash

read_methods.notes: Per OpenTune's bosch-edc17cp14 definition: calibration flashing works over OBD, but a complete original needs a bench or boot read. Bench over CAN; ecupinouts notes some bench tools also drive two auxiliary GPT lines.

notes: Higher-output VAG 2.0 TDI common-rail (EA189) ECU, about 2008-2013. The EDC17 checksum's VAG per-block constant is firmware-specific: OpenTune corrects it with the owner's stock dump as reference. ecupinouts documents a second hardware variant grounded on T94-2 instead of T94-1 - check continuity.

connectors.name: T94
connectors.description: 94-pin vehicle-side block of the 154-pin (60 + 94) Bosch connector (Transpondery: socket K)

pins.note: Only on the second hardware variant listed by ecupinouts.

bench.notes: +12 V to T94-87 (terminal 30) and T94-5 (terminal 15), ground T94-1 (T94-2 on some hardware), CAN-H T94-68 / CAN-L T94-67.
bench.resistor_notes: Put a 120 ohm resistor across CAN-H/CAN-L if your interface does not terminate (ecupinouts).

safety_note: Bench safety: use a current-limited bench supply (12-13.8 V, start with a low current limit) and a fuse in the +12 V lead; connect ground first. Confirm every pin with a multimeter on YOUR unit before applying power - ground pins should show continuity to each other (and usually the housing), and hardware revisions can differ from the sources. A CAN bus needs about 60 ohm between CAN-H and CAN-L (two 120 ohm terminations): add a 120 ohm resistor if neither the unit nor your interface terminates. Swapped CAN-H/CAN-L just gives timeouts; +12 V on a signal pin can destroy the unit.
